title: Array Slicing and Indices
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of array slicing and indices in a Swift program or workflow.
Apply collection indices in a small, inspectable example.
Check the expected result and identify one boundary case or platform constraint.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on array slicing and indices and the practical choices around it. Start with the smallest example, connect it to “Collection indices”, and verify the result before adding complexity.
content.why_it_matters: A reliable mental model of syntax, types and control flow lets you read compiler diagnostics, predict behavior and build programs in small verifiable steps.

content_blocks.title: Module 5: Collections and Data Handling
content_blocks.alt_text: Module 5: Collections and Data Handling. Lessons in order: Introduction to Swift Collections; Arrays in Swift; Array Operations; Array Slicing and Indices; Sets in Swift; Set Operations; Dictionaries in Swift; Dictionary Operations; Ranges and Collection Sequences; Higher-Order Collection Operations.

content_blocks.text: **Start with the rule.** Build a minimal example for collection indices, then inspect both the source and its result. Keep values and control flow explicit so the compiler and a reader can verify the intended behavior.

**Work through the lesson.** Select collections based on ordering, uniqueness, key-based lookup, and safe index behavior. The detailed subtopic list in this lesson preserves the curriculum coverage; treat each item as a cue for a small example or a focused question rather than trying to memorize syntax.

content_blocks.text: Use the compiler and versioned documentation as evidence. Do not treat a source-string check or an illustrative output as proof that a complete Swift program compiles on every platform.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming every Swift snippet can run in a browser or on every operating system.

common_mistakes.fix: Run command-line examples locally; use Xcode or a compatible package/target for framework-specific material.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating an illustrative output as compiler verification.
common_mistakes.why: A reference result helps reason about behavior but cannot replace compiling and testing the exact code.
common_mistakes.fix: Run the example with the stated toolchain and test one realistic edge case.

For advanced and specialist topics, check the compiler version, platform support, and official release information.
